description: Write one parameter onto the parametric object attached to each incoming space, node or segment — the flow's only way to change something that already exists on the canvas. Computes the writes live; applies them only when you press Apply.
instructions:
Every other node in the flow MAKES geometry. This one EDITS what is already on the plan, which is why it never fires on its own.

WIRING: a Spaces bundle into the geometry input (Filter by Type's Matching output is the usual source), and an ASSIGNMENT matrix into `valin-values`.

THE ASSIGNMENT MATRIX is N x 2: each row is `[indexInTheIncomingBundle, value]`. The index is position in the bundle wired in, counting from 0 — so a Math Engine that looped over those spaces in order can emit `hcat(i, result)` and it lines up. Rows whose index is out of range are dropped rather than wrapped. A space the matrix says nothing about is left alone; this never clears a parameter it was not told about.

PARAMETER KEY names the parameter to write — `direction`, `booked`, `number`. It must exist on the attached object, or that write is skipped and counted as unmatched (the readout tells you how many).

VALUE MAP turns the numbers a Math Engine can produce into the strings a SELECT parameter needs, and takes two kinds of entry in one list. A BARE WORD is positional — its place in the list is the code it names, so `North,East,South,West` writes "North" for 0 and "East" for 1. An `n=Word` entry names one specific code, which is how a sentinel outside that range gets a word: `-1=Empty,-2=Road`. Mix them freely. Leave the whole thing BLANK for a numeric or checkbox parameter and the number is written as-is. A value with no entry in a non-empty map is skipped, so a -1 meaning "undecided" writes nothing rather than defaulting to the first option.

TEMPLATE composes a STRING out of several columns, which is the only way a flow can write a formatted value — a Math Engine can put numbers on a wire and nothing else. Set it and the assignment matrix widens to `[i, v0, v1, …]`, with each `{0}`, `{1}` … replaced by that column, each passed through the value map first. `East:{0}, West:{1}, North:{2}, South:{3}` over a row `[i, 20, 21, -2, -1]` with map `-1=Empty,-2=Road` writes "East:20, West:21, North:Road, South:Empty". Blank template = the single-value behaviour above.

APPLY IS A SEPARATE, DELIBERATE STEP. The node continuously shows what it WOULD write; pressing Apply performs it as one undoable edit (Ctrl+Z restores every previous value at once). It is not part of Run Flow: Run compiles a recipe of geometry operations, and rewriting the parameters of dozens of placed objects is not something that should ride along silently with a geometry run.

IDENTITY IS RESOLVED BY POSITION IN THE CANVAS BUNDLE — the same rule Filter by Type follows — so keep this on a path that has not rebuilt the geometry. Filter, compute, write; do not Inset in between.

A space with NO attached object is skipped and counted as unmatched. Writing the value a parameter already holds is not an error, just a no-op the count still reports.

SPACES, NODES AND SEGMENTS. All three carry parametric objects, so all three can be addressed; `Host` picks which, and Auto is right whenever the bundle came straight off the Canvas node. Identity is resolved by POSITION IN THAT COLLECTION, so keep this on a path that has not rebuilt the geometry - and note that index 3 means a different element in each of the three, which is why the choice is explicit rather than inferred from the parameter name.

parameters.label: Host
parameters.help: Which canvas collection the incoming bundle addresses. Auto matches the bundle against the canvas's own arrays by reference and falls back to its shape (1 point = node, 2 = segment, 3+ = space).
